K.role: Cole peak-pressure coefficient, metric TNT fit

provenance.quote: The Cole coefficients are implementation parameters for a TNT charge (metric fit widely quoted for UNDEX work): K = 52.4 MPa, A = 1.13, K_theta = 0.084 ms, decay exponent -0.24, W in kg, R in m.

A.role: Cole peak-pressure exponent, metric TNT fit

provenance.quote: same declared implementation-parameter block (K = 52.4 MPa, A = 1.13)

K_theta.role: Cole shock-decay time coefficient, theta = K_theta W^(1/3) (W^(1/3)/R)^n

decay_exponent.role: exponent of the reduced range in the Cole decay time

T_b.role: prefactor of the bubble-pulsation period T = K_b W^(1/3)/(H + 10.33)^(5/6)

provenance.quote: UNCITED CANDIDATE: carried as a declared implementation parameter, NOT transcribed from Cole (1948).

depth_offset.role: atmospheric head expressed as metres of water (p_atm / (rho g))

provenance.quote: p_atm = 101325 Pa, rho = 1025 kg/m^3, g = 9.80665 m/s^2 -> 10.08 m; the 10.33 m figure is the fresh-water/standard value used in the law's own convention

bubble_exponent.role: exponent of the hydrostatic head in the bubble-period law

provenance.derivation: Rayleigh collapse of a gas bubble: R0 ~ (E/p_h)^(1/3) and t_c ~ R0 sqrt(rho/p_h) => t_c ~ W^(1/3) p_h^(-1/3-1/2) = W^(1/3) p_h^(-5/6); machine-checked in src/tensorfem/undex_chain.py::bubble_scaling_exponents

scaling_structure.decay_time: theta = K_theta W^(1/3) (W^(1/3)/R)^n (linear in Hopkinson scale)
scaling_structure.bubble_period: T = K_b W^(1/3) (H + 10.33)^(-5/6); the 1/3 and -5/6 exponents are derived from the Rayleigh collapse integral, only K_b is empirical

head_offset_sensitivity.judgement: the competing head conventions move T by at most 0.45 %, i.e. far inside the +/-15 % band; the convention therefore cannot rescue or break any verdict here, but it must be pinned in any citation that is deposited

independent_recompute.method: log-log least squares on a 30-point (W,R) grid and on a depth sweep; the exponent/coefficient are recovered from the values, so the recorded law is checked against itself without re-using the law's code

independent_recompute.note: agreement with recorded_values is a transcription/arithmetic check ONLY; because acquisition_status is WITHHELD it is not evidence that the physics matches Cole (1948)

probe.registry_caveat: the registry states that for A-level anchors the code-table values (including Cole's K/A) are only shown to be structurally evaluable, and that the actual table values must be transcribed verbatim from the source and registered before they may be quoted as anchor values

unit_confusion_hypotheses.what: 225 kgf/cm^2 = 22.06 MPa would be a candidate for the same printed number '225' read in a different pressure unit; it does not reproduce the probe either

the repository's K = 52.4 MPa is numerically 524 bar, i.e. self-consistent with a bar-based fit; the imperial equivalent implied by it is 21605 psi, and the often seen coefficient differs from that by a few per cent
no hypothesis can be settled from inside the ecosystem; the deposition must quote the pressure unit together with K

cross_implementation_probe.reading: two implementations of the same nominal law differ by a factor 4.29 on K at the identical reduced range; neither is traceable to a printed table, so the discrepancy cannot be resolved from inside the ecosystem -- it is the strongest single argument for the deposition listed above
